A global fit to oscillation data reproduces all mixing angles and mass splittings, predicting a maximal Dirac CP phase of $270^\circ$ and an effective Majorana mass near $15\text{ meV}$, testable by upcoming neutrinoless double-beta-decay ($0νββ$) experiments. The same coupling generates a stochastic gravitational-wave background peaking in the pulsar-timing-array and LISA bands, with peak frequency and amplitude predicted to scale as $\sinθ_{13}$ and $\sin^{-4}θ_{13}$, a falsifiable link between neutrino oscillation and gravitational-wave (GW) observations.

papers.title_en: Realization of decoherence-induced averaged symmetry-protected topological phases on quantum processors
papers.abstract_en: Symmetry-protected topological (SPT) phases are conventionally formulated for pure states protected by exact symmetries. In open quantum systems, however, decoherence generates mixed-state ensembles in which average symmetry can instead emerge only after averaging over microscopic trajectories. In this work, we realize decoherence-induced averaged SPT (ASPT) order on programmable quantum processors. Starting from a one-dimensional cluster SPT, we engineer sublattice-selective Pauli-$Z$ dephasing through ancilla-assisted quantum circuits. We observe the resulting symmetry conversion through the decay of the symmetry charge. Moreover, a two-replica Renyi-2 string correlator measured through destructive SWAP readout remains nontrivial, revealing the ASPT structure encoded at the density-matrix level. We further show that the engineered dephasing redistributes spectral weight among reduced-stabilizer sectors while preserving the characteristic twofold pairing of the half-chain entanglement spectrum. These results establish a gate-based route to engineering and probing ASPT order and demonstrate structured decoherence as a programmable resource for realizing mixed-state topological quantum matter.

papers.title_en: Snakes on a Hyper-Plane: Dynamical and Ontological Locality in Everettian Quantum Mechanics
papers.abstract_en: An apparently emerging consensus holds that Everettian Quantum Mechanics (EQM), in the Spacetime State Realism (SSR) version of Wallace and Timpson, involves ontological non-locality (i.e., non-separability) but is fully compatible with the dynamical notion of locality usually taken to be required by relativity. The claim of dynamical locality is based on the fact that the local beables postulated by the theory (namely, Reduced Density Matrices, RDMs, associated with localized regions) are not affected by interventions outside their past light cones. However, the theory's non-separability means that it posits non-local beables (namely RDMs for non-localized regions) in addition to the local ones. We argue here that the involvement of non-local beables introduces complications for extant formulations of dynamical locality and at least suggests, contrary to the emerging consensus, that SSR EQM should perhaps not be considered compatible with relativistic causality after all.

papers.title_en: Initial momentum anisotropies in the kT-factorization of the CGC I: Gradient Expansion
papers.abstract_en: We revisit single-inclusive gluon production in the dilute--dilute limit of the Color Glass Condensate and show that $k_\perp$-factorization is only the zeroth order of a systematic gradient expansion in the transverse positions of the two colliding sources, organized in powers of $1/(Q_sR)$, with $Q_s$ the saturation scale and $R$ the size over which the sources vary. Collecting terms order by order builds a ladder of scalar and tensor structures from the local distributions and their transverse derivatives, yielding an extended $k_\perp$-factorized formula that retains the spatial dependence of the sources and, through kinetic moments of the spectrum, the energy-momentum tensor. Repeating the expansion from a real-time computation of the classical Glasma fields in the future light cone reproduces the momentum-space result in the eikonal limit, but additionally retains coherent interference between amplitude and conjugate. This adds terms to the ladder (flow responses, chromo-electric--magnetic interference, and a longitudinal energy flux) further suppressed by powers of the large outgoing momentum $|\pp|\gg Q_s$. The hierarchy thus reveals momentum-space anisotropies present in the initial state before any hydrodynamic evolution, which leading $k_\perp$-factorization misses by construction. Since each order is a local operator on the same unintegrated distributions, these corrections can be added directly to existing saturation-based initial-state models, giving a dynamically generated initial momentum anisotropy and a more faithful early-time energy-momentum tensor without abandoning the tractable factorized form. Set by gradients of the transverse density profiles, they grow towards more dilute, fluctuation-dominated systems, e.g. light-ion collisions. Phenomenological consequences will be developed in a companion paper.

papers.title_en: Quantifying Margenau--Hill Nonclassicality
papers.abstract_en: Quasiprobability distributions offer a useful way of describing nonclassical features of quantum systems through their departure from classical probability theory. In this work, we investigate the quantification of nonclassicality associated with the Margenau--Hill quasiprobability (MHQ) distribution using its moments, without requiring reconstruction of the full distribution. First we introduce the logarithmic MHQ negativity as a quantifier of nonclassicality, and then derive a hierarchy of rigorous lower bounds in terms of low-order moments. Within the resulting hierarchy, the fourth-moment bound is the strongest among the bounds based on even moments. For qubits, we further derive a tight upper bound on the exact MHQ negativity and identify the corresponding extremal state. We also obtain an optimal positivity threshold based on the fourth moment for arbitrary pairs of qubit observables. Finally, we show that the relevant moments admit exact multicopy representations, providing a route to their estimation using interferometry or classical shadow techniques. Our results establish a moment-based framework for extracting quantitative information about MHQ negativity from a finite set of low-order observables.

papers.title_en: Measurement-induced remote activation of nonclassicality
papers.abstract_en: Nonclassicality, defined through nonpositivity of quasiprobability distributions such as the Wigner and Kirkwood-Dirac distributions, underlies key quantum advantages. We show that it can be remotely activated: local measurements by a correlated partner alone can drive a party whose reduced state is classical into a genuinely nonclassical conditional state. For two-qubit systems we obtain closed forms for the maximal single-branch effect and for its probability-weighted average under the best two-outcome projective measurement, the latter proven optimal over all measurements when the shared state carries no local bias. Local noise on the steered party, evaluated relative to its own noise-updated reference basis, can enhance the effect when non-unital and misaligned with that party's axis, whereas no unital channel ever helps. This nonclassicality is shown to unlock, for the same reference observable, anomalous weak values unavailable to the unsteered state under arbitrary postselection. An exactly solvable hybrid qubit-oscillator model shows the same mechanism generates Wigner negativity. These results identify measurement-induced steering as an operational resource for remotely activating nonclassicality.

papers.title_en: Design and optimization of the NSLS-II lattice with complex bend replacement
papers.abstract_en: The demand for brighter photon beams has driven the development of diffraction-limited storage rings with ultralow electron beam emittance. A complex bend (CB) lattice was recently proposed as an approach for the future NSLS-II upgrade. As a step toward this upgrade, NSLS-II plans to replace two existing electromagnetic dipoles with permanent-magnet CBs, providing the first experimental demonstration of the CB concept in a storage ring. This paper presents the linear optics design, nonlinear optimization, and machine error evaluation of the modified NSLS-II lattice. The optimized lattice provides sufficient dynamic and momentum apertures for off-axis injection and routine operation and can be corrected with the existing NSLS-II correction scheme. Scraper measurements near the planned CB installation location validate the beam aperture requirements used in the CB design.

papers.title_en: Irreducible-Mass Balance for Magnetized Null Horizons with an Internal Current Sheet
papers.abstract_en: We begin with a general question: how does the irreducible mass of a magnetized black hole change when the horizon is not stationary? The null Raychaudhuri equation gives an exact area balance for any smooth null horizon, without assuming stationarity or axisymmetry. When the horizon is axisymmetric and admits an integrable quasilocal Hamiltonian, this geometrical identity becomes an energy balance. The equation keeps area growth, rotational and electromagnetic work, nonstationary focusing, canonical-flux corrections, and internal-boundary terms separate. We then turn to Wang's self-gravitating split-monopole Blandford-Znajek engine. In the weak-field and slow-rotation regime, P/M_H≪1 and a/M_H≪1, our general balance reproduces Wang's mass- and angular-momentum loss rates. The irreducible mass, M_{irr}=√({A_H/(16π)}), reveals what those rates do not show by themselves. It measures the part of the rotational work absorbed irreversibly by the horizon. At fixed magnetic flux and under impedance matching, half of the instantaneous rotational work leaves as electromagnetic power. The other half increases the horizon area and M_{irr}. The assumptions behind this reduction are derived explicitly. A minimal nondissipative world-volume action makes the current-sheet contribution vanish through O(p^2ε^2). Direct power counting of Wang's perturbative fields, together with a compatible canonical-flux prescription, gives a relative focusing and canonical correction of O(p^2)+O(ε^2). These estimates mark the range in which the reduced Blandford-Znajek trajectory remains controlled. Extending that trajectory to high spin requires an additional extrapolation. Relating the quasilocal horizon loss to energy measured at infinity requires a separate asymptotic flux calculation.

papers.title_en: A purely mechanical system realizing a Coulomb-like interaction
papers.abstract_en: We solve in closed form a one-dimensional relativistic system: two masses interacting only through elastic collisions with a massless mediator bouncing between them. Momenta, times, and positions are hyperbolic functions of the collision index. The mediator energy, interpreted as the pair's effective potential, obeys an exact discrete Coulomb law, $V\propto 1/r$, with a Lorentz-invariant action as coupling. A massive Newtonian mediator instead transmits a $1/r^{3}$ force; one adiabatic invariant traces both laws to the mediator's dispersion relation. Continued to negative mediator energy, the closed forms turn trigonometric, binding a one-dimensional mechanical analog of the Coulomb atom.

papers.title_en: Cyclic Codes of Length 7_p^s over F_p^m + uF_p^m : Characterization, Duals, and Applications to Quantum and LCD Codes
papers.abstract_en: Let $R_2 = \mathbb{F}_{p^m} + u\mathbb{F}_{p^m}$ ($u^2 = 0$), where $p$ is an odd prime and $m, s \in \mathbb{N}$. For $p \equiv 3, 5 \pmod 7$ with $\gcd(m, 6) = 1$, the cyclotomic polynomial $Φ_7(x)$ is irreducible over $\mathbb{F}_{p^m}$. This yields a direct sum decomposition $C = C_1 \oplus C_2$ for any cyclic code $C$ of length $7p^s$ over $R_2$, where $C_1$ has length $p^s$ and $C_2$ is a $7$-cyclotomic code of length $6p^s$. We classify $7$-cyclotomic codes into four disjoint generator-based types and calculate exact cardinalities using residue and torsion subcodes. Furthermore, explicit generators for the Euclidean dual codes $C^\perp$ are determined. As operational applications of these classified codes, we construct new families of quantum stabilizer codes via the CSS framework and establish parameter criteria for linear codes with complementary duals (LCD codes).

papers.title_en: One Merger, Three Bands: Multiband Detection Rates and Parameter Estimation of Stellar-mass Binary Black Hole Coalescences from Millihertz to Kilohertz
papers.abstract_en: Stellar-mass binary black holes sweep through the millihertz, decihertz, and kilohertz gravitational-wave bands before merger, making them prime targets for multiband observations. We forecast their detection rates and parameter-estimation precision for networks combining the millihertz observatories LISA, Taiji, and TianQin; the decihertz concepts LGWA, AMIGO, and AMIGO-5; and the ground-based LVK and Cosmic Explorer. Using the binary-black-hole mass and redshift distributions inferred from GWTC-4, we first estimate the single-band yields and then account explicitly for detector lifetimes and relative mission start times when calculating multiband rates. For a signal-to-noise-ratio threshold of 8, the LISA--Taiji--TianQin network is expected to detect $53.6^{+19.7}_{-14.1}$ systems in the millihertz band, while the largest three-band yield is $23.5^{+8.7}_{-6.2}$ events for LISA--Taiji--TianQin combined with LGWA. The yield is maximized when the decihertz observation begins approximately $0$--$3\,{\rm yr}$ after the millihertz mission. Ground-informed subthreshold searches with a threshold of 5 increase the multiband yields by a factor of approximately $4$--$5$, reaching $125.1^{+46.1}_{-32.9}$ events for the same network. Fisher-matrix forecasts for a GW150914-like source show that decihertz observations provide the dominant improvement in most multiband parameter constraints, whereas millihertz data primarily sharpen the detector-frame chirp mass and sky localization. Combining the three bands improves the chirp-mass precision by orders of magnitude relative to ground-based observations alone and can reduce the localization area and coalescence-time uncertainty substantially. These results demonstrate that coordinated mission scheduling and targeted subthreshold searches are essential for realizing the scientific potential of stellar-mass multiband gravitational-wave astronomy.

papers.title_en: Quantum Sensing for Spatial Spin Noise Mapping via Nitrogen-Vacancy Magnetic Quenching in Diamond
papers.abstract_en: Detecting and mapping spin noise can reveal spatial variations in surface defect states, catalytic residues, free radicals, and spintronic materials. However, bulk measurements average over spatial heterogeneity, while scanning-probe maps require sequential rastering. Here, we demonstrate a microwave-free magnetic quenching (MQ) method for wide-field spin-noise mapping using nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centres in diamond. The protocol combines continuous LED illumination with a low-frequency, amplitude-modulated magnetic field, avoiding resonant microwave delivery or pulsed optical hardware. Field-induced spin-state mixing reduces NV photoluminescence, providing the primary contrast mechanism. We examine the response as a function of optical power and magnetic modulation amplitude, interpreting the results using a spin-state mixing model. The method is validated with aqueous gadobutrol concentration series, showing trends consistent with optically detected magnetic resonance (ODMR) measurements. We map spin-noise variations across boron nitride and single-walled carbon nanotube samples with differing defect and metallic catalyst contributions, supported by electron microscopy and spectroscopy. Notably, MQ detects a spin-noise response in boron nitride nanotubes that is silent in bulk EPR spectroscopy. This approach provides a practical framework for spatially resolved spin-noise sensing across quantum technologies and advanced functional materials.

papers.title_en: Renormalization group bounds on Araki relative entropy
papers.abstract_en: This paper derives a multiscale Bakry-Émery criterion for an upper bound on the Araki relative entropy of perturbations of an equilibrium state in relativistic QFT. Using stochastic positivity, affiliated perturbations of the relativistic bosonic field can be put in correspondence with perturbations of the massive Euclidean free field. This gives a Feynman-Kac formula, which in turns is used to derive a probabilistic expression for the Araki relative entropy. The description of the massive Euclidean free field as an abstract Wiener space provides the infinite-dimensional framework to derive a Polchinski equation. Extending the methods of Bauerschmidt, Bodineau, and Dagallier to this context yields a probabilistic bound on the Araki relative entropy, which can be formulated entirely in operator-algebraic terms. Using the criterion, it is shown that the Lorentzian massive Sine-Gordon model in the ultraviolet finite regime satisfies the relative entropy bound.

papers.title_en: Trion-mediated quantum operations on a double-dot charge qubit
papers.abstract_en: A scheme for controlling a charge qubit on a semiconductor asymmetric double quantum dot with suppressed tunnel coupling between individual quantum dots is proposed. Laser pulses convert the logical single-electron states of the qubit into auxiliary trion states, for which the resonant tunneling condition is restored due to the compensation of structural asymmetry by the Coulomb interaction of the particles. The conditions for performing orthogonal single-qubit rotations are formulated. For a two-dimensional structure, the parameters of the qubit are calculated, and the dependence of the fidelity of the inversion operation on the parameters of the laser field and the rates of dissipative processes is obtained. It is shown that the considered algorithm is characterized by high speed and reliability.

papers.title_en: \bf{PREFER} (\bf{P}olarization for \bf{F}usion \bf{E}xperiments and \bf{R}eactors: what is happening with regard to fusion with polarized fuel?
papers.abstract_en: The {\bf PREFER} ({\bf P}olarization {\bf RE}search for {\bf F}usion {\bf E}xperiments and {\bf R}eactors) collaboration aims to address the know-hows in different fields and techniques to the challenging bet on energy production by nuclear fusion with polarized fuel. The collaboration involves different institutions and researchers, sharing skills and peculiar abilities, having then possibilities to span over a variety of tasks and objectives, which are under the responsibility of the authors of this contribution, leading their groups.The collaborators, each in their own activities, starting from facing open questions in the fusion reaction physics, already reach promising results, which have also acted as an inspiration and stimulus for other groups and investigations.In the following we will report in the present status of the collaboration results and working plans, opening a window on what is being moved around.

papers.title_en: Status of experiments with polarized deuteron target at VEPP-3 electron storage ring
papers.abstract_en: A series of photonuclear experiments using a tensor-polarized deuteron target was performed at the VEPP-3 electron storage ring at the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics. The internal target setup and schematics of the photon tagging and detection systems are described. Experimental data for the tensor analyzing power component T_20 are presented for coherent and incoherent π^0 photoproduction, π^- photoproduction, and deuteron photodisintegration. New results provide a rigorous benchmark for refining theoretical models in the intermediate energy regime.

papers.title_en: Polarimetry of pulsed H−−/D−− ion beams: Extended applicability of the Lamb-shift polarimeter
papers.abstract_en: Until 2023, a polarized H$^-$/D$^-$ ion source delivered pulsed negative ion beams for stripping injection into the accelerator COSY at Forschungszentrum Jülich. Accurate and efficient measurement of the nuclear spin polarization directly behind the source is essential for precision experiments at COSY. A data acquisition system was developed to enable reliable, automated measurements with improved efficiency and to reduce operator intervention. To achieve that, the applicability of the Lamb-shift polarimeter has been successfully expanded to include pulsed H$^-$ and D$^-$ ion beams. The presented setup is useful and suitable to determine and optimize the polarization of upcoming polarized sources of the COSY type without pre-acceleration.

papers.title_en: Upgrading Polarized Beam Equipment at the JINR Accelerator Facility: Future Prospects
papers.abstract_en: At the JINR accelerator complex, within the polarization research program of the NICA project, a high-intensity SPI source of polarized deuterons and protons, low-energy polarimeters are being developed for the SPI setup at the outlet and behind the 5 MeV/nucleon linear accelerator The status, upgrades of the above facilities, future prospects are presented.

papers.title_en: Experiments at MAMI/MESA
papers.abstract_en: The Institute for Nuclear Physics at the University of Mainz operates the electron accelerator MAMI. It provides a polarized electron beam with an intensity of up to 100 𝜇A and a polarization degree of about 80%. In the near future, the superconducting energy-recovering electron accelerator MESA will be commissioned. It will deliver significantly higher beam intensities, thereby enabling a new generation of high-precision experiments. In the energy- recovery mode, for internal targets beam intensities of up to 1 mA at a beam energy of 105 MeV are planned, while for external targets operated without energy recovery, intensities of up to 150 𝜇A at 155 MeV are expected. The degree of polarization is anticipated to reach 85%. This articlereports on polarized-electron beam experiments carried out at the existing accelerator and on planned experiments at the new facility currently under construction, with a particular emphasis on the P2 experiment at MESA.

papers.title_en: Development of a Polarized H^+/D^+ Ion Source at IMP
papers.abstract_en: Polarized particle beams provide experimental access to the spin degree of freedom in nuclear and particle physics research. Utilizing spin-dependent observables, a multitude of experiments that are not achievable with conventional beam can be conducted. As part of the research and development efforts for key technologies prototyping for electron-ion collider in China (EicC), an intense spin-polarized ion source (SPIS) has been developed at the Institute of Modern Physics, Chinese Academy of Sciences (IMP, CAS). At present, SPIS can produce polarized proton (deuteron) beams with a current of 1 mA and a beam polarization of about 80% with a pulse duration of 100 microseconds at a repetition rate of 5 Hz. SPIS adopts an improved Lamb-shift polarimeter (LSP), with which the polarization of the beams extracted from the ion source can be measured directly. The integration of SPIS into high-intensity heavy ion accelerator facilities (HIAF) will enable the production of high-energy polarized ion beams, providing a powerful tool for cutting-edge physics research.

papers.title_en: Recent results of Baryon electromagnetic form factors at BESIII
papers.abstract_en: Electromagnetic form factors (EMFFs) are fundamental observables for understanding baryon structure. At the BESIII experiment, the time-like EMFFs of various baryons have been systematically investigated. The proton EMFF ratio $|G_E/G_M|$ has been precisely determined, enabling the first extraction of the $|G_E|$ lineshape, while recent neutron EMFF measurements show remarkable improvements in precision over previous experiments. Taking advantage of the self-analyzing weak decays, the relative phases of the time-like EMFFs for $\Lambda$ and $\Sigma^+$ have been measured for the first time. This non-zero phase naturally induces a transverse polarization of the final state baryons, highlighting the importance of spin observables in probing baryon structure.

papers.title_en: Measurement of the transverse momentum dependent (TMD) longitudinal single-spin asymmetry of W bosons at RHIC-STAR
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the three-dimensional spin structure of the nucleon is one of the key questions in QCD physics. Among the transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) PDFs, the TMD helicity distributions are in particular poorly constrained. Measurement of the transverse-momentum-dependent longitudinal single-spin asymmetry (\(A_L\)) of \(W\) bosons in polarized \(p + p\) collisions at RHIC provides a unique opportunity to access the flavor-separated TMD helicity distributions of quarks and antiquarks. The \(W\) bosons are identified via their leptonic decay channel (\(W \to e + \nu\)), and their full kinematics are constructed by using a recoil-based method. In this contribution, we present the motivation, analysis procedure, and preliminary results for the \(W\) \(A_L\) measurement as a function of the reconstructed \(W\) transverse momentum, based on the dataset collected by STAR in longitudinally polarized \(p + p\) collisions at \(\sqrt{s} = 510\ \mathrm{GeV}\) in 2013. These results will serve as an important input for future QCD global fits of TMD helicity distributions, especially for the poorly constrained sea-quark helicities.

papers.title_en: Measurements of $\Lambda, \Xi$ and $\Omega$ Global Polarization in Au+Au collisions at BES-II energies from RHIC-STAR
papers.abstract_en: The observation of hyperon global polarization along the system's angular momentum has revealed the existence of large vorticities in the medium created by heavy-ion collisions. In this talk, we present measurements of global polarization for $\Lambda$, $\Xi$, and $\Omega$ hyperons in Au+Au collisions at $\sqrt{s_{NN}}$ = 7.7, 9.2, 11.5, 14.6, 17.3, 19.6, and 27 GeV, based on high-statistics data collected during the RHIC Beam Energy Scan Phase II (BES-II) with the upgraded STAR detector. The comparison between $\Lambda$ and $\bar{\Lambda}$ polarizations offers potential access to magnetic-field-driven effects. The inclusion of multi-strange hyperons such as $\Xi$ and $\Omega$ introduces additional sensitivity to the later-stage dynamics of the system, placing further constraints on the properties of the QGP and the evolution of its angular momentum. These results provide new insights into the polarization mechanism and the structure of the vorticity fields in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title_en: Measurement of the transverse single spin asymmetry for forward neutral pions in (non-)diffractive like events at RHICf and STAR
papers.abstract_en: The transverse single-spin asymmetry ($A_{\mathrm{N}}$) serves as a crucial probe for understanding the mechanisms of particle production in polarized high energy particle collisions as well as the internal dynamics of quarks and gluons within a polarized nucleon. The RHICf collaboration measured a non-zero $A_{\mathrm{N}}$ for very forward ($\eta > 6$) neutral pions ($\pi^{0}$) in transversely polarized $p+p$ collisions at $\sqrt{s} = 510$ GeV within the STAR experiment. This measurement, along with a similar analysis performed at STAR for forward ($2.7 < \eta < 4.0$) $\pi^{0}$s suggests that diffractive interactions could be primarily responsible for the observed $A_{\mathrm{N}}$. To quantitatively determine the extent to which diffractive and non-diffractive processes contribute to the RHICf $A_{\mathrm{N}}$, we conduct a joint analysis of the very forward $\pi^{0}$ $A_{\mathrm{N}}$ using both RHICf and STAR detector systems from the same collisions. We report preliminary results of $\pi^{0}$ $A_{\mathrm{N}}$ in diffractive-like and non-diffractive-like event categories, and discuss the current status of this ongoing analysis.

papers.title_en: Measurement of $\Lambda/\bar{\Lambda}$ Transverse Polarization within Jets in $pp$ Collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510$ GeV
papers.abstract_en: The transverse polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons produced in unpolarized hadron–hadron collisions, first observed decades ago, remains not fully understood. Polarizing Fragmentation Functions are widely regarded as a natural framework to describe this phenomenon and can be probed through measurements of the transverse polarization of $\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}$ hyperons inside jets in $pp$ collisions, where the jet serves as a proxy for the fragmenting parton. In this contribution, we report preliminary results on $\Lambda/\overline{\Lambda}$ transverse polarization within jets in $pp$ collisions at $\sqrt{s}=510~\mathrm{GeV}$, using data collected by the STAR detector at RHIC in 2017. Comparisons with measurements at different collision energies in $pp$ collisions and with results from $e^+e^-$ annihilation enable studies of the energy-scale dependence and tests of the universality of polarizing Fragmentation Functions.

papers.title_en: Measurement of Transverse Single Spin Asymmetry $(A_N)$ of Neutral Pions $(\pi^0)$ using Transversely Polarized $p^\uparrow p$ collisions at STAR
papers.abstract_en: In proton-proton ($pp$) collisions involving a transversely polarized proton beam and an unpolarized proton beam, a left-right or azimuthal asymmetry is observed in the distribution of final-state scattered particles. The experimentally measurable quantity is known as the Transverse Single Spin Asymmetry ($A_N$). While perturbative Quantum Chromodynamics (pQCD) theory predicts very small $A_N$, experimental observations suggest otherwise. Previous measurements of $A_N$ for neutral pions ($\pi^0$) at mid-rapidity ($|\eta |< 1$) indicate that it is consistent with zero; however, at forward rapidities ($3.3 < \eta < 5.5$), significantly larger values have been observed. Consequently, measurements in the intermediate rapidity range ($1.0 < \eta < 2.0$) are crucial for providing a comprehensive understanding of $A_N$ and the underlying physics processes. The STAR Endcap Electromagnetic Calorimeter (EEMC) with a full azimuthal coverage across the pseudorapidity range of 1.1 $\leq$ $\eta$ $\leq$ 2.0 is significant for such measurements. In these proceedings, we present the preliminary results of $A_N$ for $\pi^{0}$ using the EEMC from STAR Run 2015 transversely polarized $p^{\uparrow}p$ collisions at the center-of-mass-energy of 200 GeV. The measurement has been found to be consistent within uncertainty and keeps the same trend as that of the previously published STAR measurement using Run 2006 data.

papers.title_en: An adaptive key distribution scheme based on QBER-driven and quantum-chaos synergy
papers.abstract_en: Quantum key distribution (QKD) technology provides a theoretically unconditionally secure key source for information security. However, in practical systems, noise during the transmission of quantum bits-measured by the quantum bit error rate (QBER)-can compromise key security. To address this issue, this paper proposes an encryption scheme that integrates quantum key distribution with chaotic mapping: By extracting multi-dimensional features from QBER time series, the system adaptively selects the optimal chaotic mapping and dynamically adjusts its parameters to generate a high-entropy random key stream sequence. A random forest classifier is used to intelligently select the chaotic mapping, and the effectiveness of the scheme is validated through multi-dimensional randomness measurement and security analysis. Experimental results show that the system maintains high key entropy characteristics across different noise environments, achieves a key generation rate that meets real-time communication requirements, and exhibits better resistance to known-plaintext attacks compared to traditional fixed-parameter chaotic encryption systems.

papers.title_en: Current developments of polarized sources and polarimeter at FZ Jülich and further applications
papers.abstract_en: A new theoretical concept of the quantum mechanical processes in spin filter for the separation of metastable hydrogen atoms in individual hyperfine substates enables a number of newapplications.For example, it is now possible to build a new generation of Lamb-shift polarimeter that can separate not only 𝛼 but also the 𝛽 substates with $𝑚_𝐽 = −1/2$. This opens up completely new possibilities for the search of hydrogen atoms in forbidden substates after the bound beta decay of the neutron. At the same time, corresponding simulations also provide the parameters fordesigning a Lamb-shift polarimeter for $^3𝐻𝑒^+$ ions. Furthermore, it has recently been shown that classical Lamb-shift polarimeter can determine the polarization, in addition to protons/deuteronsand 𝐻/𝐷 atoms, of $𝐻^2/𝐷^2$ molecules as well as all possible ion beam species, i.e. $𝐻^+_2 /𝐷^+_2 /𝐻𝐷^+$,$𝐻^−/𝐷^−$ or even $𝐻^+_3$. In parallel, this knowledge might help to create a new type of optically pumped polarized source by transferring a laser-induced polarization of the rotational magnetic moment to the nucleons in $𝐻_2/𝐷_2$ and $𝐻𝐷$ molecules. These techniques might also be used for the production and detectionof polarized fuel for the enhancement of the energy output of nuclear fusion reactors or the production of hyper-polarized probes in medicine.A recent application was a proof-of-principle measurement of the polarization conservation in $𝐻_2$ molecules after recombination of polarized atoms in a carbon-coated storage cell, similar to thecell that is foreseen for a planned polarized target at the LHCb experiment. In addition, in some more exotic experiments the components of a Lamb-shift polarimeter can be used to detect axionsor “dark hydrogen”.

papers.title_en: A Spin Tune Model for Spin Coherence Time Optimisation at Storage Rings
papers.abstract_en: Electric Dipole Moments (EDMs) are very sensitive probes of physics beyond the Standard Model (SM). The JEDI collaboration aims to measure the EDMs of charged particles making use of polarised beams in a storage ring. Such a precision experiment requires the maximisation of the Spin Coherence Time (SCT). To identify the working conditions that maximise the SCT, the spin tune of the single particles must be tracked with high precision. With this experiment in mind, this paper presents a model that accurately tracks the spin tune in a variety of lattices representing existing storage rings as well as a future class of dedicated storage rings. These lattices differ in the combination of electric and magnetic fields used for particle confinement and the number of sextupole families. Furthermore, the parameters used in the model are shown to be directly accessible from beam diagnostics and sextupole field strengths via linear models. Finally, the study explores the implications of the model on the decoherence of a beam stored in such storage rings. The spin tune model outcomes were verified by comparison to those of the brute force searches of configurations with SCTs of more than 1000 seconds. The result was a deeper mathematical understanding of the phenomenon as well as a method to find the setting which optimises the SCT.

papers.title_en: Determining spin effects in global equilibrium by quantum kinetic theory
papers.abstract_en: In this proceedings, we review the determination of spin effects in global equilibrium using quantum kinetic theory. Our discussion ranges from massless to massive fermions and from constant to varying electromagnetic fields. We find that by extending our consideration from constant to varying electromagnetic fields, previously indeterminate spin effects induced by vorticity and electromagnetic fields can now be further pinned down.

papers.title_en: Holographic spin alignment of vector mesons in heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract_en: We give a brief review on holographic description of spin alignment for vector mesons in strongly coupled QCD matter. Within a spectral–function framework, the spin density matrix of a vector meson is related to the in-medium current–current correlator, which we compute using gauge/gravity duality. Then we introduce the spin alignment of vector mesons in plasmas with and without magnetic fields. In particular, we find opposite signs of ($\rho_{00}^{\mathrm{H}}-1/3$) for light strange mesons and heavy charmonium, providing a strong-coupling explanation for the qualitatively different global spin alignment of $\phi$ and $J/\psi$ measured in heavy-ion collisions.

papers.title_en: Lattice QCD Calculations of Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Distributions
papers.abstract_en: Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Distributions (TMDs) provide a unique window into the three-dimensional structure of hadrons, encoding correlations between parton transverse motion and spin that are inaccessible to collinear parton distribution functions (PDFs). Lattice QCD (LQCD) offers a first-principles framework for computing TMDs, overcoming the limitations of phenomenological extractions from experimental data. This talk reviews recent progress in lattice QCD calculations of TMDs, focusing on the role of Large Momentum Effective Theory (LaMET) in connecting Euclidean lattice observables to physical lightcone TMDs. I discuss key developments in the determination of the Collins-Soper (CS) kernel, intrinsic soft functions, TMD parton distribution functions (TMDPDFs), and TMD wave functions (TMDWFs), as well as novel approaches such as the Coulomb gauge (CG) method. I also highlight ongoing challenges and future directions for lattice TMD physics, including precision determinations, gluon TMD calculations, and synergy with experimental programs and beyond.

papers.title_en: Probing Meson Structure via Lattice QCD: Electromagnetic Form Factor at High Momentum Transfer and Generalized Parton Distribution
papers.abstract_en: We present lattice QCD computations addressing crucial aspects of meson internal structure through electromagnetic form factors (EMFFs) and generalized parton distributions (GPDs). Utilizing physical masses and fine lattices, we calculate pion and kaon EMFFs at momentum transfers up to approximately 10 and 28 GeV$^2$, respectively, achieving good agreement with available experimental data at low momentum transfers and providing essential \textit{ab-initio} benchmarks for upcoming high-energy experiments. Additionally, we show the $x$-dependent valence pion GPDs at zero skewness across various momentum transfers by employing advanced renormalization and matching schemes, and also deliver a three-dimensional image of the pion structure in the impact-parameter space.

papers.title_en: The nucleon structure from an AdS/QCD model in the Veneziano limit
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the internal structure of the proton using the holographic VQCD model, which incorporates quark flavor effects and dynamically reproduces key QCD features such as confinement and linear mass spectra. Under this framework, we first compute the proton mass spectrum and corresponding wave functions, refined by including anomalous dimension corrections. Wethen evaluate proton structure functions at large Bjorken-𝑥 using a consistent set of parameters.Moreover, we derive the electromagnetic form factor of the proton by solving the equation ofmotion for the gauge field in a curved background, and show that it qualitatively aligns with resultsfrom fermion-coupled Maxwell theory. Finally, we calculate the gravitational form factors by introducing an effective graviton mass 𝑚 induced by the energy-momentum tensor of the proton andchiral symmetry breaking. Our results show remarkable consistency with available experimentaldata and lattice QCD simulations, demonstrating the HVQCD model as a reliable approach forstudying non-perturbative nucleon properties

papers.title_en: First-Principle Calculation of Collins-Soper Kernel from Quasi-Transverse-Momentum-Dependent Wave Functions
papers.abstract_en: The Collins--Soper (CS) kernel controls the rapidity evolution of transverse-momentum-dependent (TMD) parton distributions, enabling QCD factorization and connecting nucleon-structure data across scales. Its long-distance behavior at large transverse separations $b_\perp$ is still poorly constrained due to model dependence. We present a first-principles lattice QCD determination of the CS kernel at the continuum limit and physical pion mass within the large-momentum effective theory framework. Using $2+1$-flavor ensembles ($a=0.052$--$0.105~\mathrm{fm}$, $m_\pi\approx136$--$320~\mathrm{MeV}$), we compute nonlocal equal-time correlators and extract quasi-TMD wave functions. With systematic improvements---hypercubic smearing, nonperturbative renormalization, and a $b_\perp$-unexpanded matching kernel---we obtain the CS kernel in the continuum, chiral, and infinite-momentum limits up to $b_\perp\sim1~\mathrm{fm}$ with controlled uncertainties. The results match perturbative QCD at small $b_\perp$, agree with global phenomenological extractions, and can be incorporated into global fits, providing the most precise lattice constraint on the CS kernel's long-distance behavior for future TMD analyses.

papers.title_en: Global quark spin polarizations and correlations in relativistic heavy ion collisions
papers.abstract_en: Measurements by the STAR collaboration of global $\Lambda$ hyperon polarization and $\phi,K^{*0}$ meson spin alignment in heavy ion collisions have confirmed the global polarization of quark matter and indicated strong spin correlations between quarks and antiquarks. These discoveries have opened new avenues for studying quark spin correlations and the properties of QGP in high-energy physics. A systematic method has been developed to describe spin correlations in quark matter, classifying them into local and long-range correlations. It is shown that the effective quark spin correlations contain genuine spin correlations originating directly from the dynamical process as well as those induced by averaging other degrees of freedom. Based on this framework, we present a comprehensive study of spin polarization of hadrons with different spins including vector mesons, spin-1/2 hyperons and hyperon-(anti)hyperon spin correlations in heavy ion collisions. The aim of this contribution is to summarize main results and discuss future prospects.

papers.title_en: Recent Developments in perturbative calculations on DVCS
papers.abstract_en: We provide a brief review of the recent progress on the perturbative calculations of the Deeply-Virtual Compton Scattering (DVCS) process, both in the higher-order (${ O}(\alpha_s)$) and higher-power correction (${O}(1/Q)$) frontiers. This series of studies is indispensable for analyzing high-precision data from current JLAB-12 and future EIC, EIcC experiments.

papers.title_en: Small-x Spin Physics
papers.abstract_en: In this proceeding, I review recent theoretical developments in small-$x$ spin physics and discuss prospects for measurements at the upcoming Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). Topics covered include: (1) helicity evolution at small $x$ through double-logarithmic resummation and phenomenological implementations in JAMsmallx global analyses; (2) orbital angular momentum and its extraction through Generalized Parton Distributions and Wigner distributions; (3) single transverse spin asymmetries in the small-$x$ regime, including the interplay between the Sivers effect, gluon saturation, and the lensing mechanism; and (4) quantum entanglement and Bell nonlocality in deep inelastic scattering processes at the EIC. These studies demonstrate how the EIC will provide unique opportunities to probe the three-dimensional structure of nucleons, test fundamental aspects of QCD dynamics in the nonperturbative regime, and explore the quantum nature of parton interactions through entanglement measurements. Building upon the tremendous successes of the LHC and RHIC programs in unveiling the quantum nature of matter at the most fundamental level, the advent of the EIC on the horizon can unravel even more profound puzzles involving the internal structure of protons and hadrons, ushering in a precision era for nuclear and particle physics.

papers.title_en: Exploring Sivers Effects in SIDIS Vector Meson Production
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the Sivers asymmetry in the production of vector mesons, specifically $\rho^0$ and $K^*$, in SIDIS processes in the TMD factorization framework. By employing the Sivers function extracted from pion and kaon production data, we calculate the transverse single-spin asymmetry for $\rho^0$ production and compare it with recent COMPASS measurements. Our results align well with the experimental data, supporting the universality of the Sivers function across different final-state hadrons within current uncertainties. Additionally, we provide predictions for the Sivers asymmetries of $K^{*0}$ meson at the kinematics of EIC and EicC. While two types of parametrizations of the Sivers function describe COMPASS data equally well, they yield distinct predictions at EIC and EicC, indicating that future high-precision data will better constrain the Sivers function and nucleon spin structure.

papers.title_en: SIDIS off a tensor-polarized spin-1 target
papers.abstract_en: The internal structure of spin-1 hadrons, such as the deuteron, offers a unique window into nuclear dynamics inaccessible to spin-1/2 targets. In this work, we develop a theoretical framework for semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) off a tensor-polarized spin-1 target. Within the transverse momentum dependent (TMD) factorization formalism, we derive the general expression for the differential cross section. We calculate the structure functions up to twist-3 accuracy in the parton model, explicitly incorporating both quark-quark and quark-gluon-quark correlations. At tree level, we identify 21 nonvanishing structure functions expressed as convolutions of TMD parton distribution functions (PDFs) and fragmentation functions (FFs). These results establish a comprehensive foundation for future experimental studies at facilities such as JLab and the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC), where precise measurements of the deuteron tensor-polarized structure are expected.

papers.title_en: Longitudinal spin transfer to hyperon in SIDIS
papers.abstract_en: In existing fixed-target semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) experiments at the medium energies, hyperons originating from current and target fragmentation (TF) regions are not clearly distinct. We investigate the production of $\Lambda$ or $\Sigma^0$ hyperon in the SIDIS process with a polarized lepton beam and find that the spin transfer is significantly suppressed by TF contributions. As further demonstrated by a model estimation, the suppression effect from TF not only alleviates the long-standing tension between experimental data of $\Lambda$ and theoretical predictions solely based on current fragmentation, but also provides a new perspective on the hadronization mechanism.

papers.title_en: Global tensor polarization of spin-3/2 hadrons and quark spin correlations in relativistic heavy-ion collisions
papers.abstract_en: This talk summarizes our study of global polarization of spin-3/2 hadrons in relativistic heavy ion collisions. Within the quark combination model, we demonstrated how to calculate the spin density matrix of final-state hadrons and established connections between hadron polarization components and quark spin correlations. We showed that the rank-2 and rank-3 tensor polarizations of spin-3/2 hadrons are sensitive to local two-quark and three-quark spin correlations respectively. We also summarized the measurement methods for these polarization components via the angular distributions of decay products.

papers.title_en: Transverse Polarisation and Decay Dynamics of the Charmed Baryon $\Lambda^+_c$ in $e^+e^-$ Annihilations
papers.abstract_en: The study of charmed baryons provides a unique opportunity to explore the interplay between the strong and weak interactions in a regime where perturbative and non‑perturbative effects coexist. In particular, the pair production of the lightest charmed baryon, $\Lambda_c^+$, in electron–positron annihilation probes its time‑like electromagnetic form factors and opens a novel pathway to access its spin dynamics. A non‑zero relative phase between the electric and magnetic form factors generates a transverse polarisation of the produced baryon. The subsequent weak decays transfer this polarisation to daughter baryons, allowing one to measure decay asymmetry parameters, strong phase shifts and to test the $C\!P$ symmetry. This report summarises a recent measurement performed with the BESIII detector using $6.4~\mathrm{fb}^{-1}$ of $e^+e^-$ collisions at centre‑of‑mass energies from 4.60 to 4.95~GeV. The analysis establishes, for the first time, a significant transverse polarisation of $\Lambda_c^+$ in $e^+e^-\to\Lambda_c^+\bar{\Lambda}_c^-$, extracts the decay asymmetry parameters in $\Lambda_c^+\to pK_S^0$, $\Lambda\pi^+$, $\Sigma^0\pi^+$ and $\Sigma^+\pi^0$ decays, and constrains both strong and weak phase shifts. No evidence for $C\!P$ violation is observed in these Cabibbo‑favoured decays. We place the results in context by comparing them with the latest theoretical predictions and recent measurements at other experiments, including the fixed‑target charm polarisation measurement by LHCb and predictions of enhanced $C\!P$ violation in singly Cabibbo suppressed modes.

papers.title_en: Transverse momentum dependent helicity distributions
papers.abstract_en: We present the three-dimensional helicity distribution, $g_{1L}(x, k_T)$, of the proton, extracted using the azimuthal-independent longitudinal double-spin asymmetry (DSA) in semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS) processes. Utilizing data from the HERMES and CLAS collaborations, we find that the quark polarizations, defined as the ratio of the helicity distribution function to the unpolarized parton distribution function (PDF), are consistent with the predictions of Wigner rotation. Furthermore, we provide a projection study for the proposed Electron-ion Collider in China (EicC). The results demonstrate that future high-precision data from the EicC will significantly reduce the uncertainties of transverse momentum dependent helicity distributions and provide stringent constraints on the three-dimensional spin structure of the nucleon.

papers.title_en: String tension and Polyakov loop in a rotating background
papers.abstract_en: We investigate the impact of rotation on the string tension and the confinement–deconfinement transition temperature in gluodynamics using gauge/gravity duality. Rotation is introduced through two different methods, namely the global and local transformations, and the corresponding results are compared. We find that the string tension extracted from the heavy quarkonium free energy decreases as the angular velocity increases. In contrast, the transition temperature determined from the Polyakov loop exhibits an increasing behavior with angular velocity, which is consistent with lattice simulations.

papers.title_en: Polarized solid target for possible future AMBER program at CERN
papers.abstract_en: A possible physics program for the second phase of the AMBER experiment at CERN is being explored, with a focus on measurements of transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions (TMD PDFs), such as the Sivers, Transversity and Boer-Mulders functions, using a transversally polarized solid target. The COMPASS experiment previously showed that the available data favor the theoretical prediction of a sign reversal of the Sivers function between the Drell-Yan and SIDIS processes, while the question is not yet fully settled due to limited statistical accuracy. The AMBER experimental setup exploits the flexibility of the CERN SPS M2 beam line, allowing the use of both positive and negative pion beams, and foresees an increase in beam intensity, which would require upgrades to the existing polarized target system. Operation at higher beam intensities introduces challenges such as localized heating and radiation damage, potentially affecting target polarization stability. To address these issues, three possible scenarios for improvements of the polarized target system are discussed, including operation with continuous dynamic nuclear polarization during data taking or a substantial extension of the polarization relaxation time in frozen-spin mode, enabling stable measurements with higher experimental accuracy at high beam intensities. In addition, developments such as a streaming data-acquisition system and a dedicated vertex detector are expected to increase the collected statistics through a reduction of trigger dead time, while further enhancing mass resolution and background rejection, thereby extending the accessible dilepton mass range down to about 4 GeV.

papers.title_en: Bjorken-$x$ Weighted Energy-Energy Correlator: Bridging TFR and CFR
papers.abstract_en: Understanding the internal structure of the nucleon and the mechanism of hadronization constitutes a primary scientific driver for the Electron-Ion Collider (EIC). The Nucleon Energy-Energy Correlator (NEEC) offers unique advantages for this pursuit, being largely insensitive to soft radiation and immune to Sudakov suppression in the target fragmentation region (TFR). In this proceeding, based on our publication Ref. [1], we present the complete spectrum for the Bjorken-$x$ weighted EEC in DIS, spanning from the TFR to the current fragmentation region (CFR). Using the Soft-Collinear Effective Theory (SCET), we perform resummation of large logarithms up to NLL accuracy in the TFR and $\rm N^3LL$ in the TMD region. Finally, numerical predictions for EIC and CEBAF kinematics are presented, revealing a transition from the perturbative phase to a free hadron gas phase in the small-angle limit.

papers.title_en: One-Point energy correlator inside jets
papers.abstract_en: In this work, we introduce a new jet observable, the one-point energy correlators (EC), designed to characterize the in-jet energy flow distribution by measuring energy deposition at a specific angle relative to the jet axis. Building upon the transverse momentum dependent physics, we aim for the EC to provide novel insights into jet substructure and offer a new approach to study TMD physics, particularly gluon transverse momentum dependent fragmentation functions (TMDFFs) which are notoriously difficult to extract. We obtain the factorization of the EC jet function within Soft-Collinear Effective Theory and leverage the framework of semi-inclusive TMD fragmenting jet functions. We resum large global logarithms and non-global logarithms (NGLs) and show that the normalized EC jet function exhibits significantly reduced dependence on the factorization scale and is primarily sensitive to the jet scale. Finally, after incorporating non-perturbative effects, we present numerical calculations up to NNLL accuracy for global logarithms and LL accuracy for NGLs, and we compare these predictions with PYTHIA 8 simulations.

papers.title_en: Collinear Fragmentation Functions at NNLO and Constraints on the Proton PDFs
papers.abstract_en: We present the first global analysis of fragmentation functions for charged pions and kaons performed at full next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) in QCD. The analysis incorporates comprehensive world data from both single-inclusive electron-positron annihilation and semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering. We have tested collinear factorization with low-momentum-transfer data. Furthermore, we investigate how current hadron production data constrains parton distribution functions (PDFs), revealing a preference for reduced asymmetry in strange (anti-)quark PDFs as compared to NNLO PDFs derived from inclusive data analyses.

papers.title_en: Nucleon spin structure from inclusive scattering
papers.abstract_en: The year 2025 marks the centennial of the discovery of spin. In this talk, I will first recount the story of the discovery based on a lecture given by Samuel Goudsmit himself. I then review recent results from Jefferson Lab on the nucleon spin structure functions in the very low $Q^2$, and then the very high $x$ region. The latter, often referred to as the deep-valence quark region, provides a clean testing ground of various predictions for the ratio of polarized to unpolarized structure functions, and quark polarization inside the nucleon. Preliminary results from the Jefferson Lab experiment E12-06-110 on the neutron spin asymmetry $A_1^n$ up to $x=0.75$ may start to challenge predictions from relativistic constituent-quark model, perturbative QCD, and holographic light-front QCD, even after accounting for the quark orbital angular momentum.

papers.title_en: The LHCspin Project
papers.abstract_en: A polarized gaseous target, operated in combination with the high-energy and high-intensity LHC beams, has the potential to open new physics frontiers and to deepen our understanding of the strong interaction in the non-perturbative regime of QCD. Specifically, the LHCspin project aims to perform spin-physics studies in high-energy polarized fixed-target collisions using the LHCb detector. Being designed and optimized for the detection of heavy hadrons, LHCb will allow to probe the nucleon structure through, e.g., the inclusive production of c- and b-hadrons, and ideal tool to access the essentially unexplored spin-dependent gluon TMDs. This configuration will allow to explore the nucleon internal dynamics at unique kinematic conditions, including the poorly explored high x-Bjorken and high x-Feynman regimes. With the installation of the proposed setup, LHCb will become the first experiment delivering simultaneously unpolarized beam-beam collisions at 14 TeV and both polarized and unpolarized beam-target collisions at centre-of-mass energies of the order of 100 GeV. The current status of the LHCspin project is presented, with a focus on the anticipated timeline for its experimental implementation.

papers.title_en: Global fit of TMD distributions: ART25
papers.abstract_en: This study is a recent determination of transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions, fragmentation functions such as the Collins-Soper kernel. The extraction is based on a global analysis of measurements of the Drell-Yan and the semi-inclusive deeply inelastic scattering processes. The work labeled as ART25 provides a good description of the small transverse momentum spectrum of the data, is in general agreement with prior studies and incorporates technical improvements such as a flavour dependent parametrisation of the fragmentation functions anda large-𝑥 resummation for the coefficient functions connecting the distributions to their collinear counterparts.

papers.title_en: Exploring nucleon spin by Drell-Yan process
papers.abstract_en: Contributions of parton's orbital motion to the nucleon spinare encoded in the transverse-momentum dependent distributions(TMDs) and generalized parton distributions (GPDs). Currently thesedistributions are accessed through the lepton-induced processes suchas semi-inclusive deep-inelastic scattering (SIDIS) and deeplyvirtual Compton Scattering (DVCS). The (un)polarized Drell-Yanprocess with hadron beams provides a unique and complementary probe,enabling critical tests of the universality properties of TMDs andGPDs in the space-like and time-like approaches. This talk reviewsrecent results of TMDs obtained from the Drell-Yan measurements anddiscusses future prospects for accessing nucleon GPDs throughmeasurements of the exclusive pion-induced Drell-Yan process atJ-PARC.

papers.title_en: New proposal to search for T-violating $\mu^+$ polarization in $K^+\to\pi^0\mu^+\nu$ decays using stopped positive kaons
papers.abstract_en: A new experimental method to search for $T$-violating transverse muon polarization ($P_T$) in the $K^+ \rightarrow \pi^0 \mu^+ \nu$ ($K_{\mu 3}$) decay using a segmented CeF$_3$ calorimeter has been proposed. One of the key issues for this experiment is the choice of a scintillation material which can maintain the $\mu^+$ spin polarization for several $\mu^+$ lifetimes. The residual $\mu^+$ polarization in a CeF$_3$ scintillating crystal was previously measured at the J-PARC Material and Life Science Facility (MLF). The residual $\mu^+$ polarization in CeF$_3$ was measured by changing the strength of the applied longitudinal field (LF).The polarization was obtained to be 90$\pm$2\% with LF=140 Gauss, which is high enough to perform the new $T$-violation experiment.

papers.title_en: A proposal to search for T-violating muon polarization in $K^+\to\pi^0\mu^+\nu$ decay
papers.abstract_en: A new experimental method to search for T-violating transverse muon polarization($\mathrm{P}_\mathrm{t}$) in the $K^+ \to \pi^0 \mu^ + \nu $ decay has recently been proposed. In this experiment, the momentum vectors of the $\mu^+ $and the $\pi^0$, as well as the $\mu^+$polarization, are measured by a single segmented calorimeter. One of the key requirements is the choice of a scintillation material that can preserve the $\mu^+$spin polarization over several $\mu^+$ lifetimes. In addition, a high time resolution of the scintillation detector is crucial for the T-violation measurement. A test experiment to measure the $\mu^+$spin relaxation time and the timing performance of various scintillating materials was carried out at the J-PARC Material and Life Science Facility (MLF). It was found that $\mathrm{CeF}_3$ exhibits sufficiently high residual $\mu^+$polarization and a timing resolution of about 100 ps, demonstrating that $\mathrm{CeF}_3$ is well suited for the proposed T-violation experiment.

papers.title_en: Search for Electric Dipole Moments and Axions/ALPS with Polarized Hadron Beams in Storage Rings
papers.abstract_en: The project aims to address two major open questions of contemporary physics - why antimatter disappeared after the Big Bang and what dark matter is - by testing fundamental symmetries through searches for electric dipole moments (EDMs) of charged hadrons. Using polarized beams in storage rings, it targets both permanent and oscillating EDMs of protons, deuterons, and possibly helium-3, which would signal physics beyond the Standard Model. Following the milestones achieved at the COSY ring, the research will focus on developing a prototype storage ring, in both all-electric and hybrid (electric + magnetic) versions, to reach unprecedented sensitivity. Success will enable a future large-scale precision facility capable of improving current nucleonEDM limits by up to three orders of magnitude. This program has the potential to open a new precision frontier in fundamental symmetry tests and dark matter searches.

papers.title_en: $\Lambda$ Polarization in Weak-Boson-Tagged Jets as a Probe of Longitudinal Spin Transfer and Jet Quenching
papers.abstract_en: Weak-boson-tagged jets produced in unpolarized hadronic collisions are naturally longitudinally polarized owing to the chiral structure of electroweak couplings in the underlying hard partonic scattering. They therefore provide a clean and well-controlled probe of longitudinal spin transfer in hadronization, while also enabling studies of jet quenching in heavy-ion collisions using polarization as a key observable. Within collinear factorization, we present predictions for the longitudinal polarization of $\Lambda$ hyperons in $Z^0/W^\pm+\mathrm{jet}$ production in $pp$ and $AA$ collisions. We show that this observable has strong discriminating power among different flavor scenarios of the spin-transfer fragmentation function $G_{1L}$ and is also highly sensitive to jet energy loss in the QGP.

papers.title_en: Spin in Heavy-Ion Collisions: Experimental Overview
papers.abstract_en: Polarization phenomena and spin dynamics in heavy-ion collisions have attracted considerable interest since the first experimental observation of global spin polarization. Over the past few years, particle polarization has emerged as a rapidly growing field, with new measurements that have stimulated intense theoretical efforts to understand the puzzling experimental results. In this contribution, we review recent progress in experimental measurements of hyperon polarization and vector-meson spin alignment.

papers.title_en: Status of the polarized gas target for the LHCspin project
papers.abstract_en: The LHCspin project is a future experimental project to install a polarized gas target within the LHCb detector at CERN Large Hadron Collider (LHC) in order to study the internal (spin-) structure of protons and neutrons. A key requirement of the project is the development of a high-performance polarized target system, which consists of three major components: an Atomic Beam Source (ABS), a target chamber, and a polarization measurement system. The project is structured in two phases. Phase I focuses on the development of the new target system and conducting feasibility tests and preliminary measurements at the LHC Interaction Region 4 (IR4) during LHC Run 4. In Phase II, the developed target system is foreseen to be integrated into the LHCb detector at IR8 to make use of new probes in a poorly explored kinematical region for the precise measurements of quark and gluon distributions.

papers.title_en: Measurement of Anti-Quark Sivers Asymmetry at FNAL-SpinQuest
papers.abstract_en: SpinQuest at Fermilab is a fixed-target experiment to primarily measure the Drell-Yan process using transversely polarized NH$_3$ and ND$_3$ targets and unpolarized 120-GeV proton beam.In the Drell-Yan process, a quark in one scattering hadron and an anti-quark in the other hadron annihilate into a virtual photon and then decay into a muon (lepton) pair.The angular distribution of final-state muon pairs with respect to the target polarization is sensitive to the Sivers function of light anti-quarks in the nucleon, which is one of the eight leading-twist Transverse Momentum Dependent (TMD) parton distribution functions.The Sivers function of each anti-up and anti-down quarks can be extracted by the use of the NH$_3$ and ND$_3$ targets for $p$+$p$ and $p$+$d$ reactions.The intensity of the proton beam is as high as $2\times10^{12}$ protons/second, in order to accumulate the required number of Drell-Yan events.The $J/\psi$ and $\psi'$ productions are measured together, which is also sensitive to the Sivers functions of light anti-quarks and gluons.SpinQuest commissioned the target and the spectrometer with the proton beam in May-July 2024.The status of analyses of the commissioning data and preparation for the next data taking is reported.

papers.title_en: Central rapidity jet transverse single spin asymmetry measurements in proton-proton collisions with sPHENIX
papers.abstract_en: The transverse single spin asymmetry (TSSA) in inclusive jet production at mid-rapidity has been measured in 2024 using transversely polarized proton–proton collision data collected with the sPHENIX detector at the Relativistic Heavy-Ion Collider (RHIC) at a center-of-mass energy of 200 GeV. Jets are reconstructed using the full calorimeter system with the anti-𝑘$_{T}$ algorithm and a jet cone radius of 0.4. The analysis is based on an integrated luminosity of approximately 42 pb$^{-1}$, selected from a total collected luminosity of about 107 pb$.^{-1}$. The jet energy scale and resolution are corrected using Geant4-based Monte Carlo simulations, and momentum smearing effects are unfolded using an iterative Bayesian method.The TSSA is extracted from the azimuthal modulation of the jet yield asymmetry relative to the proton spin direction. The measured inclusive jet TSSA is found to be consistent with zero within statistical and systematic uncertainties over the analyzed transverse momentum range.

papers.title_en: Test of T-invariance in double polarized scattering of protons and ligthest nuclei on deuterons
papers.abstract_en: The total cross section of the interaction of transversely polarized nucleuswith tensor-polarized deuteron constitues a null-test signal ofT-reversalinvariance violation under P-parity conservation.In our papers energy dependence of this signal was calculatedusing the spin-dependent Glauber theory for pd,$^{3}$He-d and dd double polarized scatteringat rather high energies.These results are briefly reviewed herewith the main focus on the pd scattering at $\sim $GeV energies.

papers.title_en: The $b_1$ (E12-13-011) Polarized Target Experiment
papers.abstract_en: The inclusive tensor spin structure function b$_{1}$ and tensor asymmetry A$_{zz}$ will be measured in Hall C of Jefferson Lab during the E12-13-011 and E12-15-005 experiments. The University of New Hampshire Nuclear Physics Group is invested in developing the tensor enhancement techniques of selective semi-saturated RF(ssRF) and Adiabatic Fast Passage (AFP) that we will use to enhance the tensor polarization of the ND$_{3}$ target, and control systematic uncertainties of the measured asymmetries. We will use the CEBAF 11.0 GeV, 85 nA electron beam incident on the solid DNP target ($10^{38}~\mathrm{cm}^{-2}\mathrm{s}^{-1}$) and the Hall C spectrometers to measure the deuteron tensor spin asymmetries and extract b$_{1}$. In preparation for these experiments, I am analyzing Hall B Run Group C (RGC) target polarization and scattering data in order to extract the tensor asymmetry in the inclusive DIS region. I will also discuss the UNH polarized target system and polarization studies in preparation for future tensor experiments.

papers.title_en: GNN-based Track Reconstruction for MUonE Experiment
papers.abstract_en: A study of a Graph Neural Network-based model for track reconstruction in the context of MUonE experiment is presented, using simulated data corresponding to the test-run MUonE detector setup. The fully three dimensional model successfully addresses both the reconstruction and particle identification challenges essential for achieving the experiment's primary physics goal. It provides significantly faster pattern recognition than classical reconstruction algorithms, while maintaining comparable efficiency and resolution.

papers.title_en: Spin physics at HIAF
papers.abstract_en: The $\textbf{H}$igh $\textbf{I}$ntensity heavy-ion $\textbf{A}$ccelerator $\textbf{F}$acility (HIAF) will be a major workhorse for the accelerator-based (sub)atomic physics in the multi-GeV region in the next decades. As fundamental as the mass, spin plays a profound role in the structure of microscopic particles and their interactions. Besides, spin has long provided unique approaches to test fundamental symmetries and to search for new physics beyond the Standard Model of particle physics.In order to extend the discovery potential of HIAF in the fields of spin-dependent dynamics/structure and symmetry tests, developments of tools for spin-polarized experiments, such as polarized ion sources, acceleration of polarized beams and beam polarimetry, are currently ongoing. A wide range of experiments with processes $A\vec{e}$, $A\vec{p}$, $\overset{(\rightarrow)}{p}\overset{\left(\rightarrow\right)}{p}$, $\vec{p}\vec{d}$, $p\vec{e}$, $A\vec{d}$ etc. at different scales, ranging from atomic physics, over nuclear physics, down to hadron physics, can be performed at HIAF. This talk will discuss a few highlighted physical programs and related R\&D activities.

papers.title_en: Spin Physics Research INfractructure and Technologies at NICA (SPRINT@NICA)
papers.abstract_en: The study of the spin effects and polarization phenomena in hadronic reactions is the traditional scientific direction of JINR. Nowadays Spin Physics Detector at NICA as well as new spin projects at the fixed targets at Nuclotron are in preparation. This research program requires the development of high intensity polarized beams, polarized targets, beam and focal polarimetry, systems of the spin manipulation and control. The main goal of the SPRINT@NICA project is to provide the research infrastructure and to develop the technologies for the current and planned spin studies at Nuclotron/NICA. The spin transparency regime for polarized protons and deuterons over whole energy range of Nuclotron and NICA is discussed. Further development of the Source of Polarized Ions with corresponding deuteron and proton beam polarimeters is planned. The extension of the spin program to the search of axion-like particles and measurement of the electric dipole moment (EDM) with beams of polarized protons and deuterons is discussed.

papers.title_en: Spin physics and a solvable model for spin polarization
papers.abstract_en: We give a brief introduction to some models for spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions, including microscopic models, superfluid model as well as the modified blast wave model which fits the experimental data well.

papers.title_en: The First Direct Measurement of the Deuteron Electric Dipole Moment
papers.abstract_en: Permanent electric dipole moments (EDMs) of charged particles are a sensitive probe of physics beyond the Standard Model and are directly related to additional sources of CP violation that may explain the matter-antimatter asymmetry of the universe. In storage-ring experiments, the EDM of a charged particle is accessed by measuring a small tilt of the invariant spin axis relative to the plane of the ring. In this contribution, an experimental determination of the invariant spin axis at the COoler SYnchrotron (COSY), performed using an radio frequency Wien filter in combination with a superconducting Siberian snake and the 2 MV electron-cooler solenoid, is presented. The observed tilts are of the order of a few milliradians and are dominated by systematic effects which are currently under investigation. This result demonstrates the feasibility of EDM searches using storage rings and provides a basis for future dedicated facilities.

papers.title_en: Rapidity-Spectral Decomposition and Spin Dynamics in Coupled Lorentz Spacetime Coordinates
papers.abstract_en: A novel framework for parameterizing Lorentz spacetime coordinates using coupled rapidity parameters is presented, extending classical special relativity with new insights into rapidity symmetries and spin effects. Building upon the Euler–Hamilton formalism, angular and transverse rapidities are introduced, enabling spectral decompositions of relativistic dynamics into elementary functions. The relativistic dynamics is expanded into rapidity spectra, yielding a new class of Lorentz coordinates with explicit rapidity dependence. These coordinates are applied to charged particle dynamics in the fields of plane monochromatic waves and pulsed laser beams. Spin degrees of freedom are incorporated by coupling spin-precession equations with rapidity variables, yielding new spin evolution equations in 3+1 dimensions. The structure of the proper Lorentz group SO(1,3) with coupled parameters is explored, and transformations in classical, rapidity-based, and Fermi coordinates are compared. As a special case, the formalism is applied to 1+1 dimensional relativistic hydrodynamics with spin.

papers.title_en: SoLID and Future Programs at JLab
papers.abstract_en: The Solenoidal Large Intensity Device (SoLID) is a proposed new detector system for Hall A at Jefferson Lab (JLab) with a unique capability of handling high data rates by combining large acceptance and high luminosities ($10^{37}$ to 10$^{39}$ cm$^{-2}$ s$^{-1}$). SoLID at the QCD intensity frontier is the capstone of the JLab 12-GeV science with exceptional potential to lead nuclear physics research worldwide. The three sciencepillars of SoLID include imaging quarks in three-dimensional momentum space inside the nucleon with semi-inclusive deep inelastic scattering (SIDIS), extracting the nucleon mass and scalar profile densities and corresponding radii with threshold $J/\psi$ production, and searching for beyond the Standard Model physics and QCD studies with Parity-Violating DIS (PVDIS) process. Additionally, the SoLID collaboration has developed a competitive program on generalized parton distribution functions (GPDs), especially with the double deeply virtual Compton scattering (DDVCS) measurement. SoLID will provide data on all three pillars of its scientific program with unprecedented precision and sensitivity in the valence quark region. In this talk, I discuss these three science pillars together with additionally approved SoLID experiments and run-group experiments. I also present selected future programs at JLab such as the MOLLER experiment, and the proposed physics program with a polarized positron beam.

papers.title_en: Development and Testing of a 5 MeV Mott Polarimeter for Precision Measurement of Polarization for P2
papers.abstract_en: The P2 experiment at Mainz Energy-Recovering Superconducting Accelerator (MESA) aims to measure the weak-mixing angle with an uncertainty of 0.14 %. This implies that the uncertainty ofthe beam polarization measurement must be less than 1 %. To achieve this, a polarimetry chain with polarimeters operating at different energies and principles is being developed.As a part of this polarimetry chain, a 5 MeV Mott polarimeter has been fabricated, installed, and tested at the MAMI facility. The results of these tests are reported here.

papers.title_en: Toward the first experiments of T-violation search in neutron-induced compound nuclear reaction
papers.abstract_en: In a low energy region, the CP violation beyond the standard model is explored as probing violating effects of time-reversal symmetry(T-violation) in various physics systems. Neutron-induced compound nuclear reactions are interesting because the enhancement of parity-nonconservation effect(PNC) has been found in many compound nuclear states. Particularly, a Lanthanum nucleus($^{139}$La) reaches the enhancement of $10^6$ at the P-resonance of 0.75 eV. This enhancement can be also expected for the T-violating effects from recent experimental results and theoretical calculations. Additionally, this system is sensitive to a different T-violating parameter from the neutron EDM. The NOPTREX (Neutron Optical Parity and Time Reversal Experiment) collaboration is addressing several experimental issues for the T-violation search with La solid targets as a first step. One big issue is the development of a polarized La target because polarized solid targets except for protons and deuterons have not been realized yet as a practical use. We give the overview of the T-violation search in the neutron-induced compound states, present the results of experiments in the base stage with a brute-force polarized target, and then report the current status of the first stage with a dynamically-polarized target, which we call Phase-1.

papers.title_en: Final measurement of the Muon Anomalous Magnetic Moment at Fermilab
papers.abstract_en: The Muon $g-2$ Experiment at Fermilab has published the final measurement of the positive muon anomalous magnetic moment, which combines three measurements across six years of data collection. The measured value of $a_\mu$ = 1\,165\,920\,705(148) $\times 10^{-12}$ achieves a total precision of 127 parts per billion (ppb), representing more than a fourfold improvement over the previous Brookhaven National Laboratory (BNL) E821 measurement. This result is the most precise determination of the muon magnetic anomaly to date and provides a critical benchmark for testing the Standard Model at the highest precision.
